intro.title: Discover Sunny Beach Amusement Park
intro.description: Welcome to Sunny Beach Amusement Park (Лунапарк Слънчев бряг), widely recognized as the central amusement park of Sunny Beach. Located in the heart of Sunny Beach, Burgas Province, Bulgaria, this popular amusement park offers various rides and attractions for visitors of all ages.

intro.surroundingTitle: Landmarks & Attractions Around Sunny Beach Amusement Park
intro.surroundingText: When visiting Sunny Beach Amusement Park, visitors can easily explore surrounding historical landmarks and points of interest, including Nessebar Old Town (UNESCO World Heritage Site) and the Sunny Beach promenade.

visitGuide.title: Visit Tips
items: Best time to visit is during the evening when the park is lit up.
Purchase tickets online to avoid queues.
Check the weather forecast before your visit.
Bring cash for food and games.

sections.title: History & Development
sections.content: The story of the park is tied to the history of Sunny Beach itself. The Bulgarian government selected this stretch of the Burgas coast for a major seaside resort in 1958, and the area grew quickly through the 1960s and 1970s. The amusement park developed in the central pedestrian zone as the resort's entertainment centre, gradually adding roller coasters, carousels and arcade games. After the 1990s transition, the resort was modernised and the park updated with new rides and lighting. Today it stands as one of the best-known symbols of Bulgarian seaside tourism.

sections.title: Attractions & Rides
sections.content: The park offers a broad mix of rides and games. Thrill seekers can enjoy roller coasters, spinning and drop rides, while younger visitors are well served by carousels, mini trains and gentle family rides. A large arcade area offers classic prize games, and food stalls line the edges of the park. The ferris wheel provides views over the promenade and the bay. Exact attractions vary from season to season and depend on operator availability.

sections.title: Location & Access
sections.content: The park occupies a central position on Flower Street (ул. „Цветна“), the main pedestrian avenue of Sunny Beach, only a short walk from the beach promenade. The central bus station is about 800 m away, and the Old Town of Nessebar lies about 4 km to the north-east, served by local bus lines 1, 2, 5 and 8.

sections.title: Safety & Regulations
sections.content: Rides are operated under Bulgarian safety regulations and are inspected regularly. Height restrictions apply to certain thrill rides, so families should check the requirements at each attraction. We recommend supervising young children at all times and keeping personal belongings secure in crowded areas.

sections.title: Family & Children
sections.content: The park is a family-friendly destination. Many gentle rides have no height restriction and suit toddlers, while larger rides set minimum height requirements. Strollers move easily along the pedestrian zone, and staff are generally available to assist at the main attractions.

sections.title: The Park After Dark
sections.content: The park is best known after sunset. Extensive lighting, illuminated rides and the evening sea breeze create a lively atmosphere that has made it a favourite evening destination for holidaymakers. Many visitors plan their evening around a visit before or after dinner.

sections.title: Visitor Etiquette
sections.content: A little courtesy goes a long way in a busy public space. Queue at ride entrances, respect height limits and avoid reserving places on benches. Keep the area tidy by using the bins provided, and be considerate when taking photos of people.

history.title: History of Sunny Beach & the Amusement Park
history.overview: The amusement park sits at the heart of Sunny Beach, one of the oldest and largest seaside resorts on Bulgaria's Black Sea coast. Its story is inseparable from the history of the resort itself.

timeline.title: A coastline shaped by ancient civilisations
timeline.description: Long before the resort existed, the coast around Sunny Beach was home to the ancient Thracians and Greek colonists. The nearby town of Nessebar (ancient Mesembria) dates back more than 3,000 years and was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1983.

timeline.title: Sunny Beach is planned
timeline.description: In 1958 the Bulgarian government chose the coastal strip north of Burgas for a large new seaside resort. Named 'Sunny Beach' for the region's abundant sunshine, it became one of the flagship tourism projects of its era.

timeline.title: A resort for everyone
timeline.description: Hotels, promenades and leisure facilities rose rapidly along the coast. The amusement park developed in the central pedestrian zone as the resort's entertainment heart, with rides, arcades and food stalls serving a growing number of visitors.

timeline.title: Renewal and modernisation
timeline.description: After the transition of the 1990s, Sunny Beach was gradually modernised. Many hotels were renovated and new attractions added. The amusement park was refreshed with new rides and lighting, becoming the evening gathering point it is today.

timeline.title: A landmark of Bulgarian seaside tourism
timeline.description: Sunny Beach is now one of the largest Black Sea resorts in Bulgaria, welcoming millions of visitors each summer. The amusement park remains its most recognisable entertainment landmark, especially after dark.

facilities.title: Visitor Facilities Around the Park
facilities.subtitle: A neutral overview of services near Sunny Beach Amusement Park. As an independent, non-profit informational site, we describe facility types only and do not recommend specific businesses.

items.title: Public Toilets
items.description: Public restrooms are available in the pedestrian zone and near the bus station. Some may charge a small fee.

items.title: Parking
items.description: The park sits in a pedestrian area. Several paid parking lots operate nearby, including one close to the central bus station.

items.title: Dining & Snacks
items.description: The park itself hosts food stalls and snack bars, while the surrounding streets are lined with restaurants, pizzerias, grills and fast-food outlets offering local and international cuisine.

items.title: Accommodation
items.description: Sunny Beach is one of Bulgaria's largest resorts, with a wide range of hotels, aparthotels and holiday villages within easy walking distance of the park.

items.title: Shops & Convenience Stores
items.description: The pedestrian zone contains supermarkets, minimarkets, souvenir shops and pharmacies, most staying open late during the summer season.

items.title: Fuel & EV Charging
items.description: Petrol stations are located on the main roads approaching Sunny Beach. Charging points for electric vehicles are available at some stations and hotel parking areas.

items.title: First Aid & Pharmacy
items.description: A medical point and several pharmacies serve the central resort area; larger clinics and a hospital are found in Burgas. For anything serious, dial 112 (European emergency number).

items.title: Accessibility
items.description: The pedestrian promenade is step-free and largely flat, suitable for prams and wheelchairs. Individual rides have their own access rules, so ask staff at each attraction.

items.title: ATMs & Currency
items.description: ATMs and currency-exchange offices are scattered along the main promenade. Cards are widely accepted, but it is handy to keep some cash for small stalls and games.

items.title: Information & Help
items.description: Resort information points and hotel reception desks can advise on transport, tickets and local services. Park staff can point you to the nearest facilities.

items.title: Beach Access
items.description: The sandy beach is just a few minutes' walk from the park. Sunbeds, umbrellas and water-sports counters line the shore; the central beach is the busiest stretch.

legends.title: Stories, Legends & Cultural Background
legends.overview: To understand Sunny Beach Amusement Park, it helps to know the stories of the coast around it — a shoreline layered with 3,000 years of history, myth and modern ambition.

items.title: Nessebar: a city that remembers
items.text: A few kilometres from the park lies Nessebar, known in antiquity as Mesembria. Founded by Thracians and later colonised by Greeks from Megara, the city has been continuously inhabited for more than three millennia and was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1983.

items.title: The 'Unfriendly Sea' that became hospitable
items.text: Ancient Greek sailors once called the Black Sea 'Pontos Axeinos' — the Unfriendly Sea — because of its storms and unknown shores. As Greek colonisation spread along its coast, the name softened to 'Pontos Euxeinos', the Hospitable Sea, a name that still echoes in regional folklore.

items.title: Where the name 'Sunny Beach' comes from
items.text: Planned in 1958 by the Bulgarian government as a flagship seaside resort, the area was named 'Sunny Beach' for the Burgas coast's long sunny season — the region enjoys well over 2,000 hours of sunshine a year. The name soon became a brand for one of the largest resorts on the Black Sea.

items.title: A small peninsula, a 'museum city'
items.text: Nessebar is often called 'the museum city': more than 40 medieval churches once stood on its small peninsula, and traces of ancient fortifications still line its shores. On a clear evening, the silhouettes of the old town can be seen across the bay from Sunny Beach.

items.question: What are the opening hours of Sunny Beach Amusement Park?
items.answer: The park is typically open from 18:00 to 00:00 during peak season. Hours may vary depending on the season and weather conditions.

items.question: Is there an entrance fee?
items.answer: There is no entrance fee. Visitors pay per ride or can purchase a day pass for unlimited rides.

items.question: Are there food options available?
items.answer: Yes, there are several food stalls and snack bars offering a variety of options including local and international cuisine.

items.question: Is the park suitable for young children?
items.answer: Yes, the park has many rides suitable for young children, as well as family-friendly attractions.

items.question: Is there parking near Sunny Beach Amusement Park?
items.answer: The park is located in a central pedestrian zone. There are several paid parking lots nearby, for example near the Central Bus Station of Sunny Beach.

items.question: How far is the park from Nessebar?
items.answer: Nessebar is only about 4 km from Sunny Beach. You can take a local bus (lines 1, 2, 5 or 8) or a taxi to reach the amusement park in about 10–15 minutes.

items.question: Are there public toilets near the park?
items.answer: Yes. Public restrooms are available in the pedestrian zone and near the central bus station of Sunny Beach. Some may charge a small fee.

items.question: Is there somewhere to charge an electric car near Sunny Beach?
items.answer: Charging points for electric vehicles can be found at some petrol stations and hotel car parks along the main approach roads to Sunny Beach. Petrol stations are plentiful on the main roads.

transport.title: How to Get Here
transport.fromCenterDesc: Sunny Beach is about 35 km north of Burgas. By car, follow Route 9 / E87 north for roughly 35–40 minutes. By bus, Burgas Bus Station South (Автогара Юг) runs frequent services to Sunny Beach; from the Sunny Beach stop it is a short walk to the park.
transport.fromStationDesc: Sunny Beach Central Bus Station is only about 800 m from the amusement park. After alighting, walk toward the beach along Flower Street (ул. „Цветна“) for about 10 minutes; the pedestrian zone leads straight to the rides.
transport.fromAirportDesc: Burgas Airport is about 26 km away. The easiest option is a taxi or a pre-booked transfer (approx. 30 minutes). In summer, public Bus No. 10 also connects the airport with Sunny Beach; check the current timetable at the terminal.
transport.taxiDesc: Taxis are widely available at Burgas Airport, Burgas train station and across Sunny Beach. Use a licensed cab (clearly marked, with a meter) and agree the fare or check the meter before boarding. A ride from the airport to the resort centre typically takes 25–35 minutes depending on season and traffic.
transport.publicTransportDesc: Within Sunny Beach, or coming from nearby Nessebar, take local buses 1, 2, 5 or 8 and alight at the 'Center' (Център) or 'Flower Street' (Цветна) stops. Services are most frequent from May to September.
transport.walkingDesc: The park sits in the heart of Sunny Beach on Flower Street, the resort's main pedestrian promenade. If you are staying in Sunny Beach, it is an easy, flat walk from almost any hotel.
transport.drivingDesc: Set your navigation to 'Sunny Beach Amusement Park'. Because the park is inside a pedestrian zone, we suggest parking at one of the paid lots nearby (for example by the Central Bus Station) and walking the last few minutes to the entrance.

seasonal.title: Seasonal Visiting Strategy
seasonal.overview: Sunny Beach has a Black Sea coastal climate: hot, dry summers and mild, wetter winters. The patterns below are based on long-term regional climate normals (multi-decade averages), not a live forecast — always check the current weather before you set off. They help you choose the best season and what to pack.

seasons.name: Spring (Apr–Jun)
seasons.weather: Mild days of 16–24°C with breezy, changeable skies and occasional showers.
seasons.sea: The sea warms slowly and is still cool for swimming early on; the shore is quiet.
seasons.park: The park opens for the season; evenings are fresh and the promenade is calm.
seasons.tip: A light jacket for the evening and comfortable shoes for walking.

seasons.name: Summer (Jul–Aug)
seasons.weather: Hot and dry, 28–33°C by day; the park's open hours fall in the cooler evening.
seasons.sea: Warm, swimmable Black Sea (23–26°C) and busy, lively beaches.
seasons.park: Peak season — most rides run, with the longest hours and biggest crowds after sunset.
seasons.tip: Sunscreen, hat, water and a power bank; arrive early to beat queues.

seasons.name: Autumn (Sep–Oct)
seasons.weather: Warm, settled early autumn (22–27°C) cooling toward October, with fewer crowds.
seasons.sea: The sea stays pleasantly warm into September — great for beach days.
seasons.park: Still operating in early autumn with comfortable temperatures and shorter lines.
seasons.tip: Light layers and a small umbrella for the occasional shower.

seasons.name: Winter (Nov–Mar)
seasons.weather: Cool and wet, 5–11°C; the resort is largely closed and quiet.
seasons.sea: Cold, grey sea, with stormier swells possible along the coast.
seasons.park: Generally closed outside the summer season; confirm before travelling.
seasons.tip: Only plan a visit if you have confirmed seasonal opening hours.

seasonal.wildlife: The Black Sea here is a sheltered, lower-salinity basin. In summer the coastal water quality is routinely monitored by Bulgarian authorities and the resort beaches are regularly awarded Blue Flag status. Bottlenose dolphins live in these waters and are sometimes seen offshore, and the dunes and lagoons near Sunny Beach host migratory birds. We describe these as part of the local natural context and recommend following any posted guidance on swimming and protected areas.

itineraries.title: Suggested Itineraries
itineraries.overview: Flexible plans built around different travel styles. Timings assume the park's evening operating hours in peak season.

audiences.name: Families with Children
audiences.summary: A relaxed pace mixing gentle rides with breaks and the nearby beach.
steps: Arrive around opening and start with the carousel and mini-train.
Take a dinnertime break at the food stalls or a nearby restaurant.
Move to the ferris wheel and arcade games as it gets dark.
End with a short walk to the beach for the sunset.

audiences.name: Photography & Scenery
audiences.summary: Focus on the lit-up rides, the promenade and the sea at golden hour.
steps: Shoot the empty promenade and ride silhouettes just before sunset.
Capture the illuminated rides after dark from the pedestrian avenue.
Walk to the beach for blue-hour reflections on the water.
Try long exposures of the ferris wheel for light trails.

audiences.name: Low-Effort & Accessible
audiences.summary: Flat, step-free routes with plenty of seating and short distances.
steps: Enter from the central promenade — the path is flat and paved.
Use the benches along Flower Street to rest between rides.
Choose ground-level attractions and the ferris wheel for views.
Keep the beach and bus station within an easy, level walk.

general.name: Half-Day Visit
general.summary: An evening-focused plan if you have a few hours.
steps: Reach the park about 30 minutes after opening.
Prioritise 3–4 headline rides and the ferris wheel.
Grab a snack, enjoy the lights, then head to the beach.

general.name: Full-Day Visit
general.summary: Combine the beach, the old town and the park in one day.
steps: Spend the morning on the sandy beach near the park.
Have lunch on the promenade and rest during the hot midday.
Explore Nessebar Old Town (a UNESCO site) in the late afternoon.
Finish at the amusement park after sunset for the full light show.

responsibility.title: Science & Visitor Responsibility
responsibility.overview: A few notes on the local environment and how to enjoy the park and coast responsibly, as an independent non-profit guide.

items.title: Sea & Water Quality
items.text: The resort's beaches are monitored in summer and frequently meet Blue Flag standards. Follow lifeguard flags and posted advice, and avoid swimming far from supervised areas.

items.title: Local Wildlife
items.text: Dolphins, seabirds and coastal plants share this stretch of coast. Observe from a distance, do not feed wildlife, and respect fenced or protected dune areas.

items.title: Personal Safety
items.text: Follow each ride's height and health guidance, keep an eye on children in crowds, and stay hydrated in summer heat. In an emergency dial 112.

items.title: Leave No Trace
items.text: Use the bins provided around the promenade and beach, carry reusable bottles, and help keep this public space clean for everyone.

items.title: Courtesy & Etiquette
items.text: Queue patiently at rides, be mindful when photographing people, and keep noise reasonable late at night for nearby residents.

items.title: Sun & Heat
items.text: Black Sea summers are strong. Use sunscreen, shade and water, especially for children and older visitors during peak afternoon hours.
